slides.title: VIX Regime Table — Google It Right Now
The #1 Reason DIY Screeners Fail
slides.text: Running momentum screens when the VIX is above 28. Everything looks like a bounce — until it drops another 8%. Check the regime first, every single day. Skipping this step is how you blow up an account in a crash.

slides.title: SPY — Is It Above the 50-Day?
slides.caption: SPY daily chart with moving averages. Above SMA50 = bullish regime. Below = caution. Check this alongside your VIX reading every evening.

slides.question: VIX is at 31. SPY is below its 50-day MA. Which screener do you run tonight?
choices: All three — more signals is always better
slides.explanation: VIX above 28 is full Risk-Off. You run only the Oversold Bounce screener, targeting defensive sectors. Momentum and Breakout strategies in this regime produce constant false signals.

chapter.title: Strategy 1: Oversold Bounce
chapter.subtitle: Quality stocks hammered too hard — ready to snap back

slides.title: Why Oversold Bounces Work
slides.text: When a large-cap stock with solid fundamentals drops 15-20% in a week, its RSI crashes below 35. Statistically, mean reversion kicks in. Add a volume spike — institutions buying the dip — and you have a high-probability setup. The key word is quality. This only works on real companies, not speculative junk.

components.label: RSI (14)
components.detail: Oversold (<30) or Under 40 for more results

slides.title: XOM — A Textbook Oversold Setup
slides.caption: Notice the RSI dip below 35 with a volume spike — exactly what you're hunting. Large cap, high liquidity, defensive sector. This is the oversold bounce profile.

slides.title: Bookmark Your Finviz Filters
slides.text: Your filter settings live in the URL bar. Bookmark each strategy separately — 'MW Oversold', 'MW Momentum', 'MW Breakout'. Tomorrow: three clicks, three screens, five minutes. This one habit saves you from re-entering filters every single evening.

slides.question: You find a stock: RSI 22, relative volume 3.2x, but market cap is $180M. Do you trade it?
choices: Yes — RSI and volume are perfect signals
No — $180M is a micro-cap, high manipulation risk
slides.explanation: A $180M market cap is a micro-cap. Easily manipulated, poor liquidity, common pump-and-dump target. Stick to $2B+ market cap. Quality beats excitement every time.

chapter.title: Strategy 2: Momentum Expansion
chapter.subtitle: Buy strength, not weakness — with volume proof

slides.title: Counter-Intuitive But Proven
slides.text: Most beginners want to buy cheap things. Professionals buy expensive things getting more expensive. A stock above its 20-day MA with 2x normal volume is telling you: big money is committing. RSI between 50 and 70 means the move has room to run. This is momentum — and it's the bread-and-butter strategy in Risk-On markets.

slides.title: NVDA — Momentum Expansion in Action
slides.caption: Price well above SMA20, volume surging 2-3x on up-days. RSI in the 55-70 zone. This is exactly what a momentum expansion setup looks like before the next leg up.

slides.title: Never Run Momentum in Risk-Off
slides.text: VIX above 28 + SPY below SMA50 = do NOT run this screener. Momentum strategies in a crash produce textbook-looking setups that drop another 10% the next day. Check regime first. Every time.

slides.question: A stock is above SMA20, RSI at 65, relative volume 2.4x. VIX is at 14. What do you do?
choices: Skip it — RSI 65 is too high, almost overbought
Strong candidate — all three momentum signals aligned in Risk-On regime
Wait for a pullback to SMA20 first
Only trade if it's a tech stock
slides.explanation: RSI 65 is not overbought — it's in the momentum sweet spot. Above SMA20, 2.4x volume, VIX at 14 (Risk-On). All signals are aligned. This is exactly the setup you're hunting.

chapter.title: Strategy 3: Breakout Squeeze
chapter.subtitle: Catching stocks exploding through resistance — with conviction

slides.title: What Makes a Real Breakout
slides.text: A stock consolidates below resistance for weeks. Volatility compresses. Then — bang — it clears the level with 2x volume. That's a squeeze releasing. The keys: price above SMA50, new 52-week high, volume surge, and weekly volatility expanding. Without all four, it's just noise.

components.label: New High/Low
components.detail: New High — breaking out right now

components.label: View
components.detail: Switch to TA view — chart with all indicators in 3 seconds

slides.title: BTU — A Clean Breakout Pattern
slides.caption: Watch for price consolidating below a key level, then clearing it on a volume surge. SMA50 sloping up underneath. That clean move with expanding volume is the breakout squeeze setup.

slides.question: A stock hits a new 52-week high. Relative volume is 0.6 — below average. Valid breakout?
choices: Yes — new highs are always bullish
No — low volume breakouts reverse constantly
Yes — volume only matters for bounces
slides.explanation: Low-volume breakouts are one of the most common false signals. No institutional participation means no conviction. The move reverses when the retail momentum fades. Require relative volume above 1.5 every time.

chapter.title: Scoring & Selection
chapter.subtitle: From 20 results to 3 A+ trades — in 10 minutes

slides.title: The Dilution Check — 30 Seconds, Non-Negotiable
slides.text: For every stock in your top picks: Google 'TICKER dilution' or 'TICKER offering'. See ATM offering, warrants, S-3 filing, or shelf registration in the last 90 days? Remove it. Immediately. This is how we avoided the INDO disaster — technically perfect chart, but toxic financing that nuked the stock overnight.

levels.label: TP2 — sell rest
levels.value: 2× the distance to your stop loss

levels.label: Min R/R
levels.value: 1.5:1 — if math doesn't work, skip it

levels.label: Timeout
levels.value: Day 5 — close at market no matter what

slides.question: Your screens return 20 results. After scoring: 3 stocks at 8/9, 7 stocks at 5-6/9. How many do you trade?
choices: Only the 3 scoring 8+ — quality over quantity
slides.explanation: Only trade setups scoring 7 or above. The 3 stocks at 8/9 are your A-grade picks. The 5-6 scores lack confluence and have a significantly lower win rate. Selectivity is your actual edge.

slides.title: Exit Rules — When to Act vs When to Do Nothing

left.label: ACT Immediately
items: Stop loss alert fires → Sell, no debate
TP1 fires → Sell 50%, move stop to breakeven
TP2 fires → Sell remaining 50%
Day 5 timeout → Close at market, full stop

right.label: Do NOTHING
items: Price sideways → Let timeout do its job
Down 3% but stop not hit → Trust your level
Scary news but stock is fine → Ignore it
Friend says sell → Follow system, not opinions

slides.title: Your Complete DIY Scanner Checklist
items: Check VIX every evening — 30 seconds, determines everything
Bookmark 3 Finviz presets: MW Oversold, MW Momentum, MW Breakout
Run regime-appropriate screens only (not all three in Risk-Off)
Score each candidate: 3 factors, 1-3 points each — trade 7+ only
Dilution check: Google 'TICKER dilution' before any entry
Log in Google Sheets: entry, stop, TP1, TP2, timeout date
Set Yahoo/Webull alerts for every open position
Position size = capital ÷ 4 slots, fixed every trade
At TP1: sell 50%, trail stop to breakeven
At Day 5: close at market — no extensions, no excuses

slides.question: What's the biggest advantage of building your own scanner vs paying for signals?
choices: You understand WHY every trade is taken — building real skill
slides.explanation: Cost savings are real but secondary. When you build it yourself, you understand every trade. When it fails, you know why. When markets change, you adapt. A signal service keeps you dependent. Your DIY system makes you independent — and that independence is the actual edge.

slides.title: The Edge Is the Process, Not the Tool
slides.text: Professionals don't win because of better software. They win because they follow a process every single day without exception. You now have that process. Three screeners. A scoring sheet. Ironclad exit rules. 15 minutes. Zero cost. Go build it — start tonight.
